## Problem

Find Duplicate Files
Medium · Hash Table, File System, String · Company Tags · Hints

This problem is based on LeetCode 609 (Find Duplicate File in System). If you haven’t solved that one yet, it’s recommended to do so first.

In a simulated file system rooted at `"/"`, your task is to identify all groups of files that share exactly the same binary content.

Two files are considered duplicates only when their complete binary contents are byte-for-byte identical; file names and directory paths are irrelevant. The content may be large, and you can access it only as a binary stream—direct string access is not available. You need to design an efficient approach that can handle a large number of files and directories.

Implement the `DuplicateFileFinder` class:

- `DuplicateFileFinder(FileSystem fs)`  
  Constructs an instance that will operate on the given file system `fs`.

- `List<List<String>> findDuplicateFiles()`  
  Explores the file system starting from the root (`"/"`) and returns a list of duplicate groups:
  - Every group must contain **two or more** file paths whose contents are identical.
  - The order of the groups, as well as the order of paths within a group, does not matter.

The following `FileSystem` interface is provided; do **not** modify it. You can use its methods to list directory contents, determine whether a path is a directory, obtain file sizes, and open binary input streams:

```java
class FileSystem {
    /* List all files in the directory */
    List<String> listFiles(String path){...}

    /* Check if the path is a directory */
    boolean isDirectory(String path){...}

    /* Get the size of the file in bytes */
    int getFileSize(String path){...}

    /* Open the file and return a binary stream */
    InputStream openStream(String path){...}
}
```

**Constraints:**
* All files are under the root directory `"/"`.
* No two files with different sizes have identical content.
* 1 ≤ *number of files* ≤ 10⁶
* 1 ≤ *file size* ≤ 10⁹ (in bytes)
* Only files with identical content and size must be grouped as duplicates.
* You may assume standard hash utilities are **collision-free** for this problem.

**Example:**

> **Input:**
> ["DuplicateFileFinder", "findDuplicateFiles"]
> [[["/a/x.txt", "hello world"], ["/c/y.txt", "hello world"], ["/b/z.txt", "unique content"]]], []]
>
> **Output:**
> [null, [["/a/x.txt", "/c/y.txt"]]]
>
> **Explanation:**
> | File Path | Content |
> | ---------- | -------------- |
> | "/a/x.txt" | "hello world" |
> | "/c/y.txt" | "hello world" |
> | "/b/z.txt" | "unique content" |
>
> - `DuplicateFileFinder finder = new DuplicateFileFinder(fs);` // Initialize with a file system containing the specified files.
> - `finder.findDuplicateFiles();` // Returns [["/a/x.txt", "/c/y.txt"]].

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Think of each file’s content as a unique fingerprint, the challenge is grouping files by that fingerprint without reading every file’s full content multiple times.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use a hash map keyed by a content hash (e.g., SHA-256 or MD5) to cluster files, then within each cluster, compare files byte-by-byte to confirm exact duplicates, handling hash collisions.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

Target O(N) total I/O reads of each file’s content once, and watch for very large files where streaming and memory-efficient comparison matters.

</details>
